30247-mabel-s-mistake.title: Mabel'S Mistake.
30247-mabel-s-mistake.creator: Unknown
30247-mabel-s-mistake.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. It was autumn, one of those balmy Indian summer days which, if the eyes were closed, would remind you of Andalusia when the orange trees put forth their blossoms with the matured fruit still clinging to their boughs, burying its golden ripeness among cool, green leaves, and buds of fragrant snow.

49146-the-shakespeare-story-book.title: The Shakespeare Story-Book
49146-the-shakespeare-story-book.creator: Mary Macleod
49146-the-shakespeare-story-book.description: A book by Mary Macleod. questioning critic, it is a matter of small practical consequence to which the greater importance be attached by the refinements of theory. In the best plays of Shakespeare the interest evoked respectively by plot and character is so evenly balanced that he must be exceptionally short-sighted who would set the value of the one above the value of the other.

arxiv-1312-2804.title: A Novel Software Tool for Analysing NT ® File System Permissions
arxiv-1312-2804.creator: Simon Parkinson and Andrew Crampton
arxiv-1312-2804.description: Abstract Administrating and monitoring New Technology File System (NTFS) permissions can be a cumbersome and convoluted task. In today’s data rich world there has never been a more important time to ensure that data is secured against unwanted access. This paper identifies the essential and fundamental requirements of access control, highlighting the main causes of their misconfiguration within the NTFS.

arxiv-1703-04844.title: The Wigner Current for Open Quantum Systems
arxiv-1703-04844.creator: William F. Braasch, Jr., Oscar D. Friedman, Alexander J. Rimberg, and Miles P. Blencowe
arxiv-1703-04844.description: Abstract We extend the Wigner current vector field (Wigner current) construct to single bosonic mode quantum systems interacting with an environment. In terms of the Wigner function quasiprobability density and associated Wigner current, the open system quantum dynamics can be concisely expressed as a continuity equation.

arxiv-2010-13477.title: COL0RME: COvariance-based ℓ 0 \ell_{0} super-Resolution Microscopy with intensity Estimation
arxiv-2010-13477.creator: Vasiliki Stergiopoulou 1 , José Henrique de Morais Goulart 2 , Sébastien Schaub 3 Luca Calatroni 1 , and Laure Blanc-Féraud 1
arxiv-2010-13477.description: Abstract Super-resolution light microscopy overcomes the physical barriers due to light diffraction, allowing the observation of otherwise indistinguishable subcellular entities. However, the specific acquisition conditions required by state-of-the-art super-resolution methods to achieve adequate spatio-temporal resolution are often very demanding. Exploiting molecules fluctuations allows good spatio-temporal resolution live-cell imaging by means of common microscopes and conventional fluorescent dyes.

arxiv-2102-09966.title: CatNet: music source separation system with mix-audio augmentation
arxiv-2102-09966.creator: Xuchen Song*, Qiuqiang Kong*, Xingjian Du, Yuxuan Wang
arxiv-2102-09966.description: Abstract Music source separation (MSS) is the task of separating a music piece into individual sources, such as vocals and accompaniment. Recently, neural network based methods have been applied to address the MSS problem, and can be categorized into spectrogram and time-domain based methods.

arxiv-2111-11273.title: Fully commutative elements and spherical nilpotent orbits
arxiv-2111-11273.creator: Jacopo Gandini
arxiv-2111-11273.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jacopo Gandini. Let 𝔤 \mathfrak{g} be a complex simple Lie algebra, with fixed Borel subalgebra 𝔟 ⊂ 𝔤 \mathfrak{b}\subset\mathfrak{g} and with Weyl group W W . Expanding on previous work of Fan and Stembridge in the simply laced case, this note aims to study the fully commutative elements of W W , and their connections with the spherical nilpotent orbits in 𝔤 \mathfrak{g} .

arxiv-2201-06202.title: Neighboring Backdoor Attacks on Graph Convolutional Network
arxiv-2201-06202.creator: Liang Chen, Qibiao Peng, Jintang Li, Yang Liu, Jiawei Chen, Yong Li, and Zibin Zheng
arxiv-2201-06202.description: Abstract Backdoor attacks have been widely studied to hide the misclassification rules in the normal models, which are only activated when the model is aware of the specific inputs (i.e., the trigger). However, despite their success in the conventional Euclidean space, there are few studies of backdoor attacks on graph structured data.

arxiv-2302-00934.title: High-dimensional variable clustering based on maxima of a weakly dependent random process
arxiv-2302-00934.creator: Alexis Boulin, Elena Di Bernardino, Thomas Laloë, Gwladys Toulemonde
arxiv-2302-00934.description: Abstract We propose a new class of models for variable clustering called Asymptotic Independent block (AI-block) models, which defines population-level clusters based on the independence of the maxima of a multivariate stationary mixing random process among clusters. This class of models is identifiable, meaning that there exists a maximal element with a partial order between partitions, allowing for statistical inference.

arxiv-2307-04108.title: Asynchronous Proportional Response Dynamics: Convergence in Markets with Adversarial Scheduling
arxiv-2307-04108.creator: Yoav Kolumbus, Menahem Levy, Noam Nisan
arxiv-2307-04108.description: Abstract We study Proportional Response Dynamics (PRD) in linear Fisher markets, where participants act asynchronously. We model this scenario as a sequential process in which at each step, an adversary selects a subset of the players to update their bids, subject to liveness constraints.

arxiv-2403-01126.title: Single photon scattering from a chain of giant atoms coupled to a one-dimensional waveguide
arxiv-2403-01126.creator: Y. P. Peng, W. Z. Jia
arxiv-2403-01126.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Y. P. Peng, W. Z. Jia. We investigate coherent single-photon transport in a waveguide quantum electrodynamics structure containing multiple giant atoms. The single-photon scattering amplitudes are solved using a real-space method. The results give rise to a clear picture of the multi-channel scattering process.

arxiv-2405-00615.title: Chemistry in externally FUV irradiated disks in the outskirts of the Orion Nebula Cluster
arxiv-2405-00615.creator: Javiera K. Díaz-Berríos, Viviana V. Guzmán, Catherine Walsh, Karin I. Öberg, L. Ilsedore Cleeves, Elizabeth Artur de la Villarmois, John Carpenter
arxiv-2405-00615.description: Abstract Most stars are born in stellar clusters and their protoplanetary disks, which are the birthplaces of planets, can therefore be affected by the radiation of nearby massive stars. However, little is known about the chemistry of externally irradiated disks, including whether or not their properties are similar to the so–far better–studied isolated disks.

arxiv-2405-01483.title: Mantis : Interleaved Multi-Image Instruction Tuning
arxiv-2405-01483.creator: Dongfu Jiang ♣, Xuan He ♣ ♢, Huaye Zeng ♣, Cong Wei ♣, Max Ku ♣, Qian Liu ♡, Wenhu Chen ♣
arxiv-2405-01483.description: Abstract Large multimodal models (LMMs) have shown great results in single-image vision language tasks. However, their abilities to solve multi-image visual language tasks is yet to be improved. The existing LMMs like OpenFlamingo, Emu2, and Idefics gain their multi-image ability through pre-training on hundreds of millions of noisy interleaved image-text data from the web, which is neither efficient nor effective.

arxiv-2406-03051.title: Adapter-X : A Novel General Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning Framework for Vision
arxiv-2406-03051.creator: Minglei Li, Peng Ye, Yongqi Huang, Lin Zhang, Tao Chen, Tong He, Jiayuan Fan, Wanli Ouyang
arxiv-2406-03051.description: Abstract Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) has become increasingly important as foundation models continue to grow in both popularity and size. Adapter has been particularly well-received due to their potential for parameter reduction and adaptability across diverse tasks. However, striking a balance between high efficiency and robust generalization across tasks remains a challenge for adapter-based methods.

arxiv-2507-16112.title: Dissecting Reionisation with the Cosmic Star Formation and AGN Luminosity History
arxiv-2507-16112.creator: Jordan C. J. D’Silva, Simon P. Driver, Claudia D. P. Lagos, Aaron S. G. Robotham, Nathan J. Adams, Christopher J. Conselice, Brenda Frye, Nimish P. Hathi, Thomas Harvey, Anton M. Koekemoer, Rafael Ortiz III, Massimo Ricotti, Clayton Robertson, Ross M. Silver, Stephen M. Wilkins, Christopher N. A. Wi
arxiv-2507-16112.description: Abstract The combination of the z = 0 − 13.5 z=0-13.5 cosmic star formation history and active galactic nuclei (AGN) luminosity history as inferred by the James Webb Space Telescope is connected to the cosmic spectral energy distribution (CSED) to explore the sources of reionisation.

arxiv-2512-05204.title: Hardware-inspired Continuous Variables Quantum Optical Neural Networks
arxiv-2512-05204.creator: Todor Krasimirov-Ivanov, Alba Cervera-Lierta, Paolo Stornati, Federico Centrone
arxiv-2512-05204.description: Abstract Continuous-variables (CV) quantum optics is a natural formalism for neural networks (NNs) due to its ability to reproduce the information processing of such trainable interconnected systems. In quantum optics, Gaussian operators induce affine mappings on the quadratures of optical modes while non-Gaussian resources—the challenging piece for physical implementation—originate the nonlinear effects, unlocking quantum analogs of an artificial neuron.

europmc-pmc3937973.description: Background This study uses data from the World Health Organization's Study on Global Ageing and Adult Health (SAGE) to examine patterns of hypertension prevalence, awareness, treatment and control for people aged 50 years and over in China, Ghana, India, Mexico, the Russian Fede

govdocs-archive_org-nsia-KingMartinLuthe.description: UPI article by Henry P. Leifermann from Memphis on federal prisoner Humbert James Putt — ruled mentally incompetent — demanding to testify in James Earl Ray's trial with bizarre claims about the King and Kennedy assassinations.

pmc-10609088.title: Detection of SARS-CoV-2 Δ426 ORF8 Deletion Mutant Cluster in NGS Screening
pmc-10609088.creator: Riccardo Cecchetto, Emil Tonon, Nicoletta Medaina, Giona Turri, Erica Diani, Pier Paolo Piccaluga, Angela Salomoni, Michela Conti, Evelina Tacconelli, Anna Lagni, Virginia Lotti, Mosé Favarato, Davide Gibellini
pmc-10609088.description: Next-generation sequencing (NGS) from SARS-CoV-2-positive swabs collected during the last months of 2022 revealed a large deletion spanning ORF7b and ORF8 (426 nt) in six patients infected with the BA.5.1 Omicron variant. This extensive genome loss removed a large part of these two genes, maintaining in frame the first 22 aminoacids of ORF7b and the last three aminoacids of ORF8.

pmc-11272739.title: A prognostic framework for predicting lung signet ring cell carcinoma via a machine learning based cox proportional hazard model
pmc-11272739.creator: Haixin Chen, Yanyan Xu, Haowen Lin, Shibiao Wan, Lianxiang Luo
pmc-11272739.description: PurposeSignet ring cell carcinoma (SRCC) is a rare type of lung cancer. The conventional survival nomogram used to predict lung cancer performs poorly for SRCC. Therefore, a novel nomogram specifically for studying SRCC is highly required.MethodsBaseline characteristics of lung signet ring cell carcinoma were obtained from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database.

pmc-11479523.title: Targeting NUF2 suppresses gastric cancer progression through G2/M phase arrest and apoptosis induction
pmc-11479523.creator: Bo Long, Huinian Zhou, Lixia Xiao, Xiangyan Jiang, Jian Li, Zhijian Ma, Na He, Wei Xin, Boya Zhang, Xiaoqin Zhu, Zeyuan Yu, Zuoyi Jiao, Yuanyuan Ji
pmc-11479523.description: Background:Gastric cancer (GC), a malignant tumor with poor prognosis, is one of the leading causes of cancer-related deaths worldwide; consequently, identifying novel therapeutic targets is crucial for its corresponding treatment. NUF2, a component of the NDC80 kinetochore complex, promotes cancer progression in multiple malignancies.

pmc-11508519.title: Targeting Sodium in Heart Failure
pmc-11508519.creator: Filippos Triposkiadis, Andrew Xanthopoulos, John Skoularigis, Nicola Mumoli
pmc-11508519.description: A dominant event determining the course of heart failure (HF) includes the disruption of the delicate sodium (Na+) and water balance leading to (Na+) and water retention and edema formation. Although incomplete decongestion adversely affects outcomes, it is unknown whether interventions directly targeting (Na+), such as strict dietary (Na+) restriction, intravenous hypertonic saline, and diuretics, reverse this effect.

pmc-11646013.title: O068 Vascular and Autonomic Function in Comorbid Insomnia and Sleep Apnoea
pmc-11646013.creator: B Tong, G Stewart, J Flood, P de Chazal, P Cistulli
pmc-11646013.description: Comorbid insomnia and sleep apnoea (COMISA) is a common sleep disorder and may be associated with increased cardiovascular risk. This study aimed to compare polysomnography-derived biomarkers of cardiovascular risk in patients with COMISA, obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) only, insomnia only, and without OSA or insomnia.Patients were identified from the Sydney Sleep Biobank database.

pmc-12563393.title: Proof-of-Concept Digital-Physical Workflow for Clear Aligner Manufacturing
pmc-12563393.creator: Shih-Hao Huang, I-Chiang Chou, Mayur Jiyalal Prajapati, Yu-Hsiang Wang, Po-Kai Le, Cho-Pei Jiang, Andrea Scribante
pmc-12563393.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background/Objectives: Clear aligner therapy has become a mainstream alternative to fixed orthodontics due to its versatility. However, the variability in thermoforming and the limited validation of digital workflows remain major barriers to reproducibility and predictability. Methods: This study addresses that gap by presenting a proof-of-concept digital workflow for clear aligner manufacturing by integrating additive manufacturing (AM), thermoforming simulation, and finite element analysis (FEA). Dental models were 3D-printed and thermoformed under clinically relevant pressures (400 kPa positive and −90 kPa negative).

pmc-12745302.title: “Anyone Else Struggling with Work-Genocide Balance?” Exploring the Psychological and Social Impact of Collective Annihilation in Gaza
pmc-12745302.creator: Federica Cavazzoni, Ala’ Mustafa, Cindy Sousa, Ola H Abuward, Mona Ameen Nofal, Guido Veronese
pmc-12745302.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This study investigates the psychological and social impact of the ongoing colonial violence in Gaza, both on the local population and on distant witnesses. Drawing on 30 testimonies collected between November 2023 and June 2024, the research captures the lived experiences from two distinct groups: 15 Palestinian participants living in the Gaza Strip, and 15 mental health professionals (including psychotherapists and academics) based in Europe.

pmc-13309372.title: SIRT3/AARS2 regulates SOD2 lactylation to determine neuronal fate in TBI
pmc-13309372.creator: Jiazhi Song, Jing Liu, Wenjun Fan, Fang Gou, Hong Yang, Ping Wang, XiaoKun Yang, Kai Tao

pmc-13314987.title: Simultaneous measurement of linear and angular displacement sensor using POF based on macro-bend loss
pmc-13314987.creator: Liu Liu, Ma Rui, Abdul Ghaffar, Muhammad Saleh Urf Kumail Haider, Kamran Ali, Muhammad Asghar Khan, Md. Rajibul Islam, Md Shohel Sayeed
pmc-13314987.description: This paper presents a plastic optical fiber-based sensor for simultaneous linear and angular displacement measurement through intensity modulation of macro-bend loss. The sensing mechanism relies on generating bend-induced losses in twisted fiber probes and coupling the attenuated light into receiving fibers.

pmc-13446754.title: Pharmacist-Led Discharge Care to Reduce Postdischarge Health Care Utilization
pmc-13446754.creator: Joshua M. Pevnick, Korey Kennelty, An T. Nguyen, Kallie Amer, Carl T. Berdahl, Galen Cook-Wiens, John Fanikos, Julie Fiskio, Hiroshi Gotanda, James Guan, Andrew J. Henreid, Michelle S. Keller, Eunji M. Ko, Donna W. Leang, Yervant Malkhasian, Lina Matta, Dylan Moriarty, Logan Murry, Annie Muske, Tery
pmc-13446754.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This randomized clinical trial examines whether pharmacist-led transitions-of-care interventions after hospital discharge reduce subsequent readmissions and other health care utilization among patients aged 55 years or older with polypharmacy. Introduction

The rate of posthospitalization adverse drug events (ADEs) among older adults has been estimated at 4% to 37%,1,2 with recent rates of 5% to 6% found in 2 large medication management clinical trials.3,4 Posthospitalization ADEs can result in serious morbidity or death.

pmc-13569714.title: Clinical Impact of Target‐Mediated Drug Disposition of Small Molecules with Focus on Early Phase I Study Designs
pmc-13569714.creator: Francesca Tessaro, Neil John Parrott, Matthias B Wittwer, Franziska Schaedeli Stark, Andrés Olivares‐Morales, Michael Derks, Stefan Sturm
pmc-13569714.description: stinct exposure‐response relationships, TMDD can introduce safety risks and complicate dose regimen selection. This perspective emphasizes the importance of early identification of TMDD and integration of quantitative pharmacology approaches to inform development strategy, mitigate risks, and support data‐driven decision‐making in early‐phase clinical studies.

pmc-13590255.title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence Integration in Medical Student Education in Somalia and Low-Resource Settings: A Context-Sensitive Implementation Framework
pmc-13590255.creator: Mohamed Mohamud Ali, Abdullahi Abdirahman Omar
pmc-13590255.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly generative AI and large language models, is increasingly used by health-professions learners for explanation, revision, simulation, feedback, and assessment support, while institutional governance has not always kept pace. Somalia is a distinctive setting in which recent mapping identified 112 health-professions schools, many concentrated in urban areas, while medical education continues to face unequal access to faculty, simulation, standardized assessment, and reliable digital infrastructure.

pmc-13627696.title: Spontaneous aging of mature amyloids alters structural stability, cytotoxicity, and susceptibility to biological clearance
pmc-13627696.creator: Maksim I Sulatsky, Olga V Stepanenko, Arina A Kayda, Olesya V Stepanenko, Ekaterina V Mikhailova, Anna I Sulatskaya
pmc-13627696.description: Accumulation of amyloid fibrils is a key factor in the pathogenesis of progressive diseases, including neurodegenerative disorders such as Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s disease, as well as systemic amyloidosis. Although amyloid deposits are known to persist in vivo for years or even decades, it remains unclear how the structure and biological properties of mature fibrils evolve during prolonged post-assembly residence.
